newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ESSEX STAY TOP DESPITE DEFEAT BY SOMERSET.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ESSEX STAY TOP DESPITE DEFEAT BY SOMERSET.

text.p: Mike Burns hit an impressive 83 from 90 balls to lead Somerset to a four-wicket victory over Sunday League leaders Essex.
Burns struck his best score in the competition as eighth-placed Somerset reached their target of 210 with 16 balls to spare.
Burns had earlier performed admirably in the role of medium-pacer, taking two for 28 from six overs.
But it was leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed who proved the most successful Somerset bowler. His three for 36 included the valuable wicket of Stuart Law, who had made a speedy 43 off 36 balls.
Despite the defeat Essex remained top but Kent drew level on points after a two-run win over Northamptonshire.
Matthew Fleming was Kent's match-winner, dismissing the dangerous David Sales and then running out Jeremy Snape in the final over.
Kent had scored 209 for eight, with openers Trevor Ward and Matthew Walker each making 40.
Lancashire remained level on points with the leading pair in third place after blowing the chance to go top when they tied with Middlesex.
Gary Yates and Darren Shadford scrambled a bye off the final ball to leave Lancashire on 197 for nine, one short of the victory which would have put them first.
